name: Hashbaddanah
overview: Hashbaddanah was a male Levite who played a role in the public reading of the Law during the time of Ezra. He is specifically noted for standing on Ezra's left hand as the Law was read, an event that implies his Levite heritage. This positioning highlights his involvement in the religious reforms and teaching of the Mosaic Law among the returned exiles.
namesAndTitles: The name Hashbaddanah likely means 'YHWH has considered me,' reflecting a theophoric element common in Hebrew names. This proper name is recorded in Nehemiah 8:4 and does not appear to have been given directly by God but carries significant meaning related to divine attention or care.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture indicates that Hashbaddanah was a descendant of the tribe of Levi, inferred from his role during the reading of the Law. Beyond this tribal affiliation, no additional family relationships are recorded in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Hashbaddanah's significance lies in his participation during a pivotal moment when Ezra publicly read the Law to the people, marking a renewal of covenant faithfulness among Israel after the exile. His position beside Ezra underscores the Levites' role in supporting the teaching and preservation of God's Word. This event, recorded in Nehemiah 8:4, highlights the communal and priestly involvement in restoring proper worship and adherence to the Law.
